cards.text: King Josiah of Judah heard the Book of the Law read, and he tore his clothes (2 Kings 22:11). The prophetess Huldah said the LORD would bring calamity on this place and its people, but Josiah's eyes would not see it (2 Kings 22:16, 20). Then the king summons all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

cards.question: Only the elders Josiah summoned go up with him to the house of the LORD.
In the hearing of everyone, Josiah ___ all the words of the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.
Then Josiah stands by the pillar before the LORD. What does he make there?

answers.text: A covenant to follow the LORD
A plan to rebuild the city walls
A vow to never go to war

cards.question: Josiah makes the covenant to follow the LORD by himself, and the people stay out of it.

cards.text: Friend, when I promise to scrub my ovens, I scrub ONE and sit down for a week. Not Josiah. He gives orders to Hilkiah the high priest, the priests second in rank and the doorkeepers.

cards.question: What does Josiah order Hilkiah and the priests to remove from the temple of the LORD?

answers.text: The articles made for Baal and Asherah
The timber bought for the repairs

cards.text: He burns them outside Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron and carries their ashes to Bethel. Not even the ASHES get to stay in town, friend.

cards.question: Josiah also does away with the priests the kings of Judah had ordained for the high places. What had those priests been doing?

answers.text: Burning incense to the sun and moon

cards.text: Next up is the Asherah pole. Josiah brings it out of the house of the LORD, down to the Kidron Valley outside Jerusalem.

cards.question: What does Josiah do to the Asherah pole in the Kidron Valley?

answers.text: Burns it and grinds it to powder
Buries it deep in the valley
Sends it back to its makers

cards.text: Then he throws its dust on the graves of the common people. Burned, POWDERED and scattered, that pole is not coming back for a sequel, friend, because there's not enough left of it for a CAMEO.
He also tears down the quarters of the male shrine prostitutes that were in the house of the LORD, where the women had woven tapestries for Asherah.
Then Josiah brings all the priests in from the cities of Judah. EVERY one of them, and I bet that's the group chat nobody wanted to get added to.

cards.question: From Geba to Beersheba, Josiah ___ the high places where the priests from the cities of Judah had burned incense.

cards.text: He even tears down the high places of the gates at the entrance of the gate of Joshua, the governor of the city. That gate sits to the left of the city gate, and now those high places are gone.

cards.question: The priests of the high places don't come up to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem.

cards.text: Still, they eat unleavened bread with their fellow priests. Not at the altar, friend, but still at the table.
Josiah keeps going. Next he desecrates Topheth, a place in the Valley of Ben-hinnom.

cards.question: Why does Josiah desecrate Topheth in the Valley of Ben-hinnom?

answers.text: So no one could sacrifice a child to Molech
So no army could camp in the valley
So no one could build houses there

cards.text: Then Josiah removes the horses the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun from the entrance to the house of the LORD. Horses for the SUN, friend, right at the LORD's front door.

cards.question: Josiah keeps the chariots of the sun for his own army.

cards.text: Josiah burns up the chariots of the sun. Those chariots are officially OFF the road, friend.

The kings of Judah put altars on the ROOF, friend, by the upper chamber of Ahaz, an earlier king of Judah (2 Kings 16:1). And Manasseh, Josiah's grandfather, had set up altars in the two courtyards of the house of the LORD (2 Kings 21:18, 26).

cards.question: Josiah pulls down the altars on the roof and the ones Manasseh set up in the two courtyards. He ___ them there and throws their dust into the Kidron Valley.

cards.text: Then he desecrates the high places east of Jerusalem, south of the Mount of Corruption. They were built for Ashtoreth, Chemosh and Milcom, the abominations of the Sidonians, the Moabites and the Ammonites.

cards.question: Which king of Israel had built those high places for Ashtoreth, Chemosh and Milcom?
After smashing the sacred pillars and cutting down the Asherah poles, Josiah covers the sites with human bones.

cards.text: Josiah even pulls down the altar at Bethel, the high place set up by Jeroboam son of Nebat, a king of Israel (1 Kings 12:20), who had caused Israel to sin. Then he burns the high place and grinds it to powder.

cards.question: At Bethel, Josiah leaves the Asherah pole standing.
At Bethel, Josiah turns and sees tombs on the hillside. What does he do with the bones inside them?

answers.text: Burns them on the altar to defile it

cards.text: This happens according to the word of the LORD proclaimed by the man of God who had foretold these things. That man had called out Josiah by name long before (1 Kings 13:2).
Then something on that hillside catches the king's eye. He asks, “What is this monument I see?”

cards.question: Josiah asks about a monument at Bethel. Whose tomb do the men of the city say it is?

answers.text: The man of God who came from Judah

cards.question: Josiah orders the bones in the man of God's tomb burned on the altar too.

cards.text: Josiah says, “Let him rest,” and, “Do not let anyone disturb his bones.” So they leave his bones undisturbed, along with those of the prophet who had come from Samaria.

cards.question: In the cities of Samaria, what does Josiah do with the shrines of the high places?

answers.text: Removes them all just as at Bethel
Leaves them standing for the people
Hands them over to the priests

cards.text: On the altars he slaughters all the priests of the high places and burns human bones on them, and then he returns to Jerusalem. That's where we'll pause, friend, because Josiah's story isn't done yet.
